submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the word that presents the clause it opens as an inference from what has just been read: strongest on result/consequence connectives (Therefore, Hence, Thus, Consequently, As a result, so, thereby, resulting in, which meant, 'This means'), about half as strong on the reason and concessive/contrast linkers that bind a clause back to the previous one (because, since, although, whereas, however, yet, nevertheless). It stays at baseline on additive and purely temporal sequencers (and, also, moreover, in addition, meanwhile, later, temporal 'then'), on a subordinator whose main clause has not yet arrived ('Although the sample was small, ...'), and on ordinary content words; a minority of peaks fall on the comma of a quoted reply, which this account leaves open.

rival_explanations: Resultative-only: the pole is a detector of consequence adverbs (therefore, hence, thus, consequently, as a result) and its peaks on reason and concessive linkers are incidental, so it predicts that because, since, although, however and yet stay near baseline on new text.

Generic connective detector: the pole fires on any clause-linking connective or sentence-initial discourse adverb, additive ones included, so it predicts that moreover, furthermore, additionally, in addition and also fire as strongly as therefore on new text.

Stance/rarity marker: the pole fires on low-frequency sentence-initial stance adverbs of any kind (Hence, Presumably, Naturally, Of course, In fact) rather than on the relation being one of consequence, which predicts those fire as strongly as Therefore while frequent because/although stay low.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The tunnel flooded during the storm on Tuesday night. Therefore, the morning deliveries had to be rerouted over the pass above the valley.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel prose holdout: sentence-initial 'Therefore' presents the rerouting as the consequence of Tuesday's flooding, the strongest class the hypothesis names.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Almost a third of the respondents left the final question blank. Hence the totals for that item should be read with caution.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The consequence connective 'Hence' draws the caution from the blank responses in the previous sentence, and it sits mid-probe so its token is measured.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cooperative had run the same three ovens, installed in the nineteen sixties, and its bread had won prizes at county shows for as long as anyone could remember. When the health inspector visited in March she found the flues clogged with decades of soot and asked for a written plan within thirty days. The committee met on the first Tuesday of April, argued for two hours about the cost of new ducting, and voted at last to borrow the money from the regional fund. The work took eleven days. During that time the bakers used the old wood-fired oven in the yard, which could take only forty loaves at a time, and wholesale customers were told to expect shorter deliveries. Most of them agreed to wait. On the morning the new flues were lit for the first time, the smoke that had hung over the yard for years was gone. Consequently, the cooperative was able to raise its daily output by half within a month.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context holdout: 'Consequently' appears deep in a passage and sums up a chain of prior events as its consequence, testing whether the pole still fires when the premise is far back.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The county cut the bus subsidy in June. As a result, two rural routes now run on weekdays only.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A multiword result connective in a novel policy context, predicted strong by the hypothesis even though its surface form differs from the single adverbs.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Doubling the radius multiplies the area by four. Thus a pipe of twice the width carries four times the water at the same pressure.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Mathematical 'Thus' presenting the pipe result as derived from the previous sentence; a claimed trigger in a topic absent from the top examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The pressure gauge climbed past the red line, so the operator shut the main valve before the pipe split.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Coordinating 'so' mid-sentence, binding the shutdown back to the rising gauge as its consequence; the hypothesis lists 'so' as a strongest-class trigger in any position.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The volunteers cleared the drainage channel before the rains, resulting in far less flooding along the lower street this winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Participial result marker 'resulting in' with the consequence in the same clause, testing the claimed trigger outside sentence-initial position.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
# The cache is keyed by content digest,
# thereby avoiding collisions between files that happen to share a name.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Code-comment holdout in a different syntax role: 'thereby' still marks the collision avoidance as the consequence of the keying, so the hypothesis predicts a peak inside a comment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee turned down the proposal because its cost figures had been prepared by the firm that stood to win the contract.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Reason linker 'because' binding the rejection back to the previous clause, which the hypothesis rates at about half strength, so it is predicted elevated and this separates it from the resultative-only rival.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The first field trial showed no measurable change. However, the second used twice the dose and did produce one.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Concessive 'However' at the start of a contrastive clause that binds back to the first trial, predicted active at roughly half the result-connective strength.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The library stayed open until nine all summer. Moreover, it added a quiet study room on the third floor.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Additive 'Moreover' adds a fact without presenting it as inferred from the previous sentence, which the hypothesis puts at baseline while the generic-connective rival fires.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The panel doubted the budget figures. Furthermore, it questioned whether the timetable could be met at all.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Second additive probe with 'Furthermore' so the additive class is not judged on one sentence; hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The rain eased just before dusk and the crowd drifted back toward the stage, shaking the water from their blankets.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Plain coordinating 'and' joining two clauses with no inferential link, named by the hypothesis as baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Engineers replaced the pump through the afternoon. Meanwhile, a second crew repaired the antenna on the roof.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Temporal sequencer 'Meanwhile' places two events side by side without consequence, a class the hypothesis explicitly puts at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They loaded the van in the yard, then drove north until the fuel gauge touched empty near the county line.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Temporal 'then' sequencing two events, listed by the hypothesis as baseline; a near-miss for a clause-ordering connective.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The guests finished dinner around ten. Afterwards, a few of them walked down to the harbour to watch the boats.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Purely temporal 'Afterwards' orders two events with no inference, so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The foreman expected trouble on the first morning. Although the mill had been idle for years, the machinery started on the first attempt.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Fronted concessive subordinator whose main clause has not yet arrived at the peak token, the exact case the hypothesis says stays at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Even though the ferry was cancelled, most of the delegates reached the conference by midday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Second fronted concessive, testing that the baseline holds for 'Even though' and not only the hypothesis's own wording.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The mill has stood beside the river since eighteen seventy-four; its wheel still turns for visitors on Sunday afternoons.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token in another part of speech: 'since' as a temporal preposition, not a reason linker, so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The nurse turned the monitor toward the wall. She lowered her voice so the child in the next room would not wake.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Purpose 'so' introduces an intention rather than a consequence, a different sense of a claimed trigger that the hypothesis does not cover as a result connective.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The studio sells its shelving unpainted. Buyers are free to arrange the units however they prefer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token in another part of speech: 'however' as a manner adverb inside a subordinate clause, not the contrastive linker the hypothesis rates at half strength.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The harbour master watched the barometer all evening. The ship had not yet cleared the harbour when the storm broke.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'yet' in its 'still' sense is a temporal adverb, not the concessive linker the hypothesis lists, so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The agency rewrote every headline that autumn. The style guide now bans the word therefore from marketing copy.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Metalinguistic mention: the trigger token is named as a word rather than used to present a clause as an inference, so the hypothesis predicts baseline while a lexical consequence-adverb detector would fire on the token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee met in the small room behind the library. In fact, the room had no heating at all that winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Sentence-initial stance adverb 'In fact' adds an aside and marks no consequence, reason or contrast relation, which is where the hypothesis and the stance/rarity rival disagree.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The hall was half empty when the chair called for the vote. Frankly, nobody expected the motion to pass at the spring meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A rare sentence-initial speech-act adverb 'Frankly' expresses the speaker's attitude rather than inferring the clause from the preceding text, separating the hypothesis from the stance/rarity rival.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Three barges unloaded timber at the quay before dawn. Gulls circled the masts; a man swept the stone steps; the tide turned at seven.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Ordinary content words and no clause-linking connective at all, the baseline class the hypothesis names.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The stall sold bread, cheese, olives, and a few jars of honey brought up from the next village.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Delimiter control: a list comma carries punctuation but no quoted reply and no inferential content, so the hypothesis predicts baseline on it.
Syntax-role change: the trigger word is an identifier in code rather than a discourse connective, so the hypothesis predicts baseline.
Syntax-role change: the trigger appears as string data returned by a function, presenting no clause at all, so the hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The village hall had been built in nineteen twenty-eight with money raised at a summer fete, and for most of its life it was the only indoor space in the parish. By the time the roof began to leak in twenty nineteen, the committee had already spent two years arguing about whether to repair the building or replace it on the same plot. A surveyor's report that spring put the cost of a new roof at less than half the cost of demolition and rebuilding, which settled the argument quickly enough. Work began in September and was finished before Christmas, with the scaffolding taken down two days before the carol service. The floor was sanded and resealed at the same time, and the kitchen was refitted with a new sink and two second-hand cookers. Moreover, the committee persuaded the county to resurface the path from the road to the main door, which had been a hazard for years.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context additive near-miss: 'Moreover' deep in a passage adds a further fact rather than inferring it from the preceding account, and it matches the length of the long positive holdout.
